speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens when you wake up frightened? Do you remember having a nightmare, or do you feel scared without knowing why?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since she is not confused and can be consoled, this sounds more like nightmares than night terrors. Does she remember the specific scary content of the dreams when she wakes up?

Also, has she been under any unusual stress at school or at home recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
She recalls the dreams and exhibits bedtime procrastination, which strongly supports a diagnosis of nightmare disorder often linked to stress or anxiety. I will request a sleep study to rule out other sleep disorders and check for any underlying sleep apnea or restless leg syndrome that might be disrupting her sleep architecture.

REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
